name: probe-new-predicate-at-empty-test
description: A new predicate quantified over all tests of a sheaf can be a fact about the index type; probe it at the empty test before refuting it
metadata:

---

Before treating a refutation of a newly-defined predicate as a finding, instantiate the
predicate at the **empty test**. A condition of the form "for every test `S`, distinct
indices never share a value" over a sheaf collapses: the sheaf's value at an empty scheme is
terminal (subcanonical/bot-cover), so every family satisfies the shared-value premise there,
and the condition is equivalent to `Subsingleton ι` — a fact about the index type, mentioning
the family without constraining it.

**Why:** I defined `IndexSeparated f` this way in AJCR's `Pic0ChartMultiIndexInterval.lean`,
built a file around refuting it at a two-chart family whose members were injective, and
concluded that overlapping charts are what evades a no-go. All the theorems were true. The
headline was inverted: the mechanism was not that overlapping charts refute the hypothesis,
it was that the hypothesis could never transmit anything about the maps. The injectivity of
the witness family did no work in the refutation — the same proof refutes it at any two
indices. This is [[vacuity-lives-in-the-conclusion]] one level out: every binder named the
family and the predicate was still about `ι`.

**How to apply:** on a sheaf-valued predicate, write the `iff Subsingleton ι` probe (or the
`iff True` probe) *first*, as a theorem, before building consumers. If it closes, restrict to
tests carrying a point — usually free, since the argument that consumes the predicate produces
a test containing the point it started from. Then check the restriction is not a slower
vacuity by exhibiting a witness at two distinct indices, and record what the witness costs: a
witness using an empty source proves satisfiability without saying the real object can be
arranged that way. Keep the collapsed form in the file as a named theorem so nobody restates
it. Related: [[nonvacuity-witness-must-satisfy-the-binders]],
